title: 3.7.23 Array Methods
description: Eight multiple-choice questions on .map(), .slice(), .concat(), spread, rest, and mutating versus non-mutating methods. Checked instantly.

questions.question: What does [1, 2, 3].map((n) => n * n) produce?
questions.explanation: .map() applies the callback to each element and collects the results into a new array of the same length. It never combines the results into one number; that would be .reduce().

questions.question: After const b = a.map((n) => n * 2); what has happened to a?
options: It now holds the doubled values
It is now the same array as b
questions.explanation: .map() builds a new array and leaves the original alone, which is why the result has to be assigned to a variable to be kept at all.

questions.question: What does ["a", "b", "c", "d", "e"].slice(1, 3) return?
questions.explanation: .slice(start, end) includes start but not end, so slice(1, 3) copies positions 1 and 2: ["b", "c"]. The count is end - start.

questions.question: Why is calling .slice() with no arguments useful?
options: It sorts the array in place
It makes a full, genuinely separate copy of the array
It converts the array to a string
questions.explanation: .slice() with no arguments copies from start to finish into a new array, so changes to the copy do not affect the original. Assigning const copy = original would only give a second name for the same array.

questions.question: When a and b are both arrays, what are the differences between a.push(b) and a.concat(b)?
options: push changes a and adds b as one nested item; concat leaves a alone and returns a new flat array
concat changes a and push does not
push returns a new array and concat changes a
questions.explanation: Two differences at once. push mutates a and nests the array argument, giving [1, 2, [3, 4]]; concat leaves both alone and flattens one level, giving [1, 2, 3, 4].

questions.question: Why does Math.max([3, 9, 4]) give NaN, and what one change fixes it?
options: Math.max cannot handle numbers above 9; sort first
It received one argument that is an array, not a number; spread it as Math.max(...numbers)
The array must be joined into a string first
Math.max needs four arguments, not three
questions.explanation: Math.max compares the separate arguments it is given. Handed a single array it tries to treat that array as a number and gets NaN. Spreading the array supplies the elements as individual arguments.

questions.question: What is { ...base, size: 10 } when base is { size: 4, color: "red" }?
options: An error, because size appears twice
questions.explanation: The spread copies every property of base in, then the later entry size: 10 overwrites the copied size: 4. Duplicate keys are not an error: the last one wins, which is why the override must come after the spread.

questions.question: Which pair correctly names one method that changes the array it is called on and one that does not?
questions.explanation: .sort() and .reverse() reorder the array in place, changing the original. .map(), .slice() and .concat() return something new and leave the input alone.
